Feature Maturity Matrix

Current position (2026-11-15, sa_plugin_sla@60d8bfc3): SA text is the only production path — sa sla build and sa sla build-exe (default / auto / --test-backend sa) all first emit .sa text, which the host Flattener then parses to complete the backend. SAB structured artifacts were sealed on 2026-11-15 (tag sab-sealed-2026-11-15) and are positioned as an optimization direction: they are enabled only on explicit opt-in (--test-backend sab or sa sla sab ...), and their equivalence maintenance with the text path is no longer advanced. Since 2026-09-28 (sa_plugin_sla@e96e6b3) the SAB compatibility fallback has been removed; uncovered features explicitly report UnsupportedSabDirectFeature and fail loudly, with no more silent fallback. In the first table below, the two rows sa sla check / sa sla build-exe are the overall end-to-end maturity (which also holds for the default text path); the remaining metrics and the two tables "entered / not yet entered the direct path" record the coverage snapshot of this sealed optimization path (direct SAB), for reference when opting in as needed; they do not represent the capability ceiling of the default production path.

Overall metrics (change with versions; the repository documents are authoritative)

MetricSnapshot valueMeaning
sa sla check306/313The proportion of demos the frontend (lexical/syntax/types) can take in
sa sla build-exe239/313 (about 76%)The real maturity of end-to-end compilation to a native executable
Direct-only sweep200/200 (both backends' results consistent, 2026-09-29, sa_plugin_sla@f5f473b)The number of unit tests consistent across both backends after the fallback removal; SLA_SAB_NO_FALLBACK is now defunct
Y/shared-lowering72%The share of lowering logic implemented through shared lowering rules
Direct SAB fallback-removal100% (fallback removed, no fallback path)The SAB compilation coverage that does not take the SA compatibility fallback

The roughly 22-percentage-point gap between the two reflects the gap between "the frontend can parse it" and "the backend lowering can land it"; the performance bottleneck used to be mainly on the fallback path (2026-07 snapshot; the fallback was removed on 2026-09-28).

Features that have entered the direct SAB fast path

  • Function and @test declarations; parameters, let, return, expression statements
  • The basic type mappings of i*/u*/int/bool/void/pointers and borrows
  • Phase 1 scalar var x: T: stack_alloc + store/load, supporting reads after branch merging; identifier assignment and basic while
  • Integer/boolean literals, binary arithmetic/comparison/bitwise operations
  • Direct function calls (multiple parameters); function pointer values and calls (vtable const + call_indirect)
  • Ordinary closure binding and calling (inline body + parameter register mapping)
  • Plain struct literals, field access, and the general layout lowering of struct returns
  • The basic control flow of if/else to br/label/jmp/merge
  • Chained / value-producing if let (including && chains)
  • The planned static-call &[T; N] -> &[T] array-to-slice borrowing
  • panic(code); the register metadata needed for scope leak checking
  • The first batch of std surface metadata bridging (sla_std/std_surface.sla_meta): associated functions/methods/index sugar expanded into imported SA macro fragments

Features not yet in the direct path (fallback removed; uncovered means explicit failure)

FeatureCurrent stateOwning Phase
Enum payload / match extractionTag/payload layout not fully in the direct pathPhase 5
@derive semanticsThe operator/function calls generated by derive are not covered by directPhase 5
Struct update ..base / spaceship comparisonAggregate update, copying, and operator dispatch not covered by directPhase 5
The for in protocol (collection iteration)Both the non-generic protocol and generic specialization await landingPhase 6
async/await state machinesSingle await, two awaits, join2, linear three/four consecutive awaits (cross-stage local values preserved), and some dynamic Pending/Ready already have direct-SAB lowering; nested awaits across async fn boundaries fail on both backends (a shared-layer gap, not a divergence; rosetta 314/315 fail for this reason, see 09_async); the unified executor/reactor is still a polling macroPhase 8 (partially done)
Collection-class std metadata (Set, etc.), nested contract importsstd surface gapsPhase 4
Call materialization such as dyn trait objects + Rc combinationsThe shared call/argument materialization plan is still convergingPhase 3/4

Known language-level limitations

  • &mut T/&mut self not yet introduced (Phase 2 plan); currently &self covers both reads and writes, with the SA Referee as backstop;
  • No drop keyword/function; lifetime cleanup is fully managed;
  • The demos/rosetta tree is a sample set compared against Rust reference implementations; not all of it passes end to end, and it must be verified individually as needed;
  • SAB v4 does not keep the per-instruction original .sa text; use sa sla sab disasm for debugging.

Investigation means

The fallback has been removed, so uncovered features fail loudly by default; to locate a gap, use SLA_SAB_TRACE_UNSUPPORTED=1 to see the first missing point:

# 在安装了 sa 与 sla 插件的环境运行
SLA_SAB_TRACE_UNSUPPORTED=1 SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla test <file.sla> --test-backend sab --filter "..."
SLA_PROFILE=1 SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla test <file.sla> --trace-panic
WarningThe values in the tables above are snapshots from when the documents were written and change quickly as versions advance. Before making a decision, check the repository's docs/roadmap_status_cn.md and docs/sab_pipeline_cn.md.
